chapter: Central Avenue clubs, Nordskog, Sheffield and Music Town
title: Building the Watts Country Club
summary: He built a large dance hall on 116th Street in the county, moved the Dreamland furnishings there, added a merry-go-round, and featured Jelly Roll for a time.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: And then, when did you open the Watts Country Club?
About six months after that. I went out there, and bought two or three lots and built a big dance hall. Yeah, built the building from the ground up.
Ohhh, that was...where was it located?
On 116th Street, I think. On this side was Los Angeles city. On that side was the county, so we were in the county, and
we danced till four or five o'clock in the morning. Yeah.
No, it...down near Long Beach [Boulevard], east of the Long Beach streetcar.
Long Beach Boulevard. 116th Street near Long Beach Boulevard. So you had the Watts Country Club and the Dreamland Cafe running simultaneously...
Yeah, well, it took about that long to build it, you see. But we moved all the stuff from Dreamland out there. Chairs and tables and things.
And this was a dance hall? Is that right--the Country Club? Or...

A big dance hall, yeah, and I [laughs] got the papers over there. I had a merry-go-round out there for the kids, and I had concessions--drinks and souvenirs on the outside that a couple of fellows rented for--you know, they sold souvenirs and things on the outside --was going to have a regular little park out there but it didn't pan out so good.
Mostly holidays daytime--afternoon--but the rest of it was generally Saturday nights, Sunday nights.
And who worked it? Did you have a band in there, or what band worked there?
No, I had Jelly Roll in there for awhile, and then different bands after that. Jelly Roll went away.
